summary: Found and fixed the root trigger behind the 'nonstop DOS command windows' a user hit after restoring a backup and restarting: child processes (ffmpeg, ffprobe, python vision worker, nvidia-smi, tar, powershell) were spawned without suppressing their console window on Windows. A console child whose parent has no console of its own — the state a detached/relaunched app or a Windows service is in — gets a brand-new console window allocated on every spawn; the per-camera stream/recording pipeline retrying a failing ffmpeg (e.g. restored camera URLs that don't resolve on the new machine) then spammed windows without end. Added infra/procutil.HideWindow(cmd) — sets CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows, no-op elsewhere — and applied it to every exec.Cmd across infra/recording (capture, remux, clip extract, ffprobe duration/codec, TRIM/Optimize-Volume), infra/stream (live-view ffmpeg), infra/rtsp (MJPEG fallback, snapshots), infra/vision (one-shot + persistent detector workers), infra/externaltools (version probes), and the apps/mymatasan/services ffmpeg/python installers, LPR/training runners, and GPU detection. Complements the earlier apphost self-restart hardening (CREATE_NO_WINDOW on the relaunch + storm guard).
compatibility: No API/behavior change; Windows-only effect (child console windows are hidden). Child stdout/stderr are still captured via pipes, so no logging/output is lost. HideWindow is a no-op on Linux/macOS. New package infra/procutil.
